subject: Pilot cost & TCO — batching/caching levers, budget gates and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@fastledger.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot cost & TCO — batching/caching levers, budget gates and proposed next steps

Alicia — great conversation earlier. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move to the procurement/finance steps you mentioned. I’ve attached a light cost model and the proposed MVP scope.

Top pain points you confirmed:
- High per-request cost on transactional prompts (avg 1.2k tokens/request) driving unpredictability against an annual budget cap.
- Latency SLOs for checkout flows (p99 under 300ms) — important for customer conversion.
- Security/audit requirements (data residency + short retention windows) that push toward a dedicated or VPC deployment.

Goals we agreed:
1) Prove the feature in a 6-week pilot with bounded spend (target pilot budget: $60k)
2) Achieve ~40–60% unit-cost reduction via batching + prefix/KV caching and moving non-critical embeddings offline
3) Keep p99 latency within 300–350ms in pilot (accepting small variance for caching priming)

Cost/TCO levers we recommended (summary):
- Model variant: run a mixed routing policy — high-accuracy model for critical checkout prompts, a cheaper quantized variant for follow-ups.
- Batching: continuous micro-batching for background pipelines; 100–200ms batching window on low-latency flows to capture 10–20% savings without violating SLOs.
- KV/prefix caching: cache common prompts and recurrent user context (5–20% hit rate expected from your telemetry), reduces decoder tokens and overall unit cost.
- Offline work: embeddings and heavy reranking moved to scheduled jobs where possible.

Attached: redwood-pilot-cost-model.xlsx (sheet with three scenarios: conservative / expected / aggressive), and MVP scope (mvp-scope.pdf).

Proposed next steps (actionable):
1) I’ll update the cost model with your exact monthly request volume and sample token distributions — you’d provide last 30-day token histogram and a list of 10 representative prompt templates (Alicia).
2) FastLedger procurement to share standard PO/contract path and an initial procurement contact (Procurement).
3) Technical kickoff with your infra lead to confirm VPC/networking and KMS requirements — we propose Wed, Jul 8 at 10am PT.

If that plan works I’ll lock the pilot parameters (duration, budget cap, rollback path, and success criteria) into a mutual action plan and send a short SOW + pricing addendum for the $60k pilot.

Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

— Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the clear recap and for the files. High level: this matches our internal read. A few notes/questions: 

1) Token histogram & prompts: I can share last 14 days of anonymized telemetry and 8 prompt templates by EOD Monday. Are CSV exports fine?
2) Pilot budget: $60k is in the ballpark; procurement will confirm whether we need a PO or a signed SOW first. I’ve looped procurement.
3) Latency: we’ll try the Wed slot for technical kickoff but might need to move to Thu — procurement needs to confirm availability.

Two quick asks: can you show a short sensitivity table in the cost model that highlights breakpoints for 20%, 40%, 60% caching hit rates? That will help our finance team understand downside. Also include a run-rate extrapolation post-pilot (12-month) for the expected and conservative scenarios.

Appreciate it — Alicia
